cells.tense: You are standing on ground you have been gathering toward, and the direction still holds.
cells.act: mark the good thing together, out loud
cells.ask: Say the good of it plainly, once, no speech, to whoever the good belongs to — then let it stand there with them.
cells.core:
You have been gathering toward something, and by now the direction holds. What you defended was worth defending, and here, it has come through. That is rare enough to be spoken, and it is not the same as boasting: the thing you held got held with help, and the ones who helped already know what it cost.

Sharing it is the part that is yours to give. Next time the finished thing is in your hands and the ones who carried it beside you are nearby, say the good of it plainly — once, no speech, no round of thanks to manage. Marking a thing in front of others is not the same as keeping it. What you gathered, they gathered too, and saying so gives it somewhere to go.
cells.sheetLine: The direction held. Say so where it can be heard.
cells.verb: holding gathered ground against what pushes back
cells.place: where a finished thing gets released into what comes next

cells.tense: You are bracing against resistance that has not arrived, and rehearsing the fight in advance.
cells.act: sit still until the calibration settles
cells.ask: Find an hour where nothing is actually wrong and put the problem down untouched. Sit with it, or walk with it. Change nothing until the hour is up.
cells.core:
You are holding a line, and you are holding it early. The defense has been running so long that rest reads as a threat — if you put it down, something might get through. It feels like vigilance. From outside, it looks like you fighting battles on next week's field.

Pushing harder is not the correction. Genuine engagement comes from feeling, and feeling needs a still hour to arrive in. Pick one where nothing is actually wrong, and stop adjusting: sit with the problem, or walk with it, and decide nothing until the time is up. What you are defending will keep. What is real will be what is unchanged when you come back.
cells.sheetLine: You are defending ground nobody is attacking yet.

cells.tense: You are still standing at a door you already walked through, holding it open.
cells.ask: The new shape has landed. Do the small thing that keeps it where it sits — the shelf back on its bracket, the hour kept, the room left as it stands.
cells.core:
Something required your resolution, and you met it. Then the moment passed, and you stayed where you were — in the change itself, still gripping the handle. The direction you chose has already won; what is missing is the ordinary ground under it.

The sustaining work is small and does not need the old push. Once this week, do one thing that keeps the new arrangement where it landed: put it back where it belongs, keep the hour you said you would, leave the room as it stands. That is the whole task. The change asked for an ending; this only asks that what it made stay made.
cells.sheetLine: The door is behind you. The new shape needs holding, not the old push.

cells.tense: You are holding a line nobody asked you to hold, and you say it was circumstance.
cells.act: build the first new thing from what the clearing showed
cells.ask: Build one small true thing with your hands on the cleared ground — first step only. Keep going whether or not anyone is watching.
cells.core:
You kept something standing through pressure, and when it was over you said you had just gone along with it. The defense was yours. The call to hold was yours. The pressure was large and your part was quiet, so you filed it under circumstance — but the gathering was done by you.

The road back runs through the same work at a smaller scale. Something cleared; you know what it was. On that ground, build one true thing with your hands this week, small enough to finish or to leave unfinished, and count it as yours. Then build the next. Skilled work is where your part becomes visible again, and you have the skill; you have been using it and calling it nothing.
cells.sheetLine: You held the line. The choice was yours, not circumstance.

attempts.check: Unsupported claim: that there is a specific person or community the celebratory act belongs to — the record gives the medicine's acts but not that a 'them' exists, so the ask must make the sharing optional in form (say it out loud, to whoever it belongs to) rather than presume a recipient. Reader objection: a Bound signature defending direction may not feel like celebration at all; the balanced cell could read as imposed. The ask survives being wrong: 'say the good thing out loud' still teaches something even if the read misses, because it does not require an audience or a mood. Sentence serving the writer more than the person: 'the momentum holds' — cut the aphorism; it sounds earned but tells them nothing they can do.
